notes.s: A pep talk that says set the whole mess on fire and stop apologising for it.
notes.t: Title track of the 2016 repackage 화양연화 Young Forever, and the song that turned BTS concerts into a jumping ritual. It answers the anxiety of the earlier singles with noise instead of comfort. The spoon line landed in the exact year Korean twentysomethings were arguing online about inherited class, and it got heard as a direct reply to that argument. The dance break and the bow-wow-wow chant are what the fandom knows it for.
k: 수저 is a spoon, and in mid-2010s Korea it meant the one you were born holding. 금수저 is a gold spoon for inherited money, 흙수저 a dirt spoon for none. The ending -길래 asks what gives you the standing to say that, so the line is: what kind of spoon are you, exactly, to be talking.

-거리다 bolts onto a repeated root and means to keep doing that, usually to the speaker's annoyance. Spoon-spoon-ing means they will not shut up about spoons. Same machinery gives 비틀거리다 to keep staggering, which shows up as 비틀대며 in line 4, and 수군거리다 to keep whispering about someone.

The ending -네 is for noticing something as it happens, closer to look at it burn than to it burns. So the title is a bystander's remark, while the hook's 싹 다 불태워라 switches to -어라, the bluntest imperative Korean has. The song moves from watching to ordering inside two lines.

살어 and 말어 should be 살아 and 말아. Swapping the 아 for 어 is a southeastern regional colour that rap borrows for swagger, roughly what dropping a g does in English. 멋대로 means however you please, and it usually carries a shrug of disapproval that is deliberately absent here.
